stemMd: Which is most analogous to the author's preferred use of a digital reconstruction?

options.label: A
options.textMd: An editor declares all later annotations worthless.

options.label: B
options.textMd: An editor destroys the manuscript after making a transcript.

options.label: C
options.textMd: An editor silently replaces uncertain words with preferred readings.

options.label: D
options.textMd: An editor refuses to protect a crumbling page.

options.label: E
options.textMd: An editor prints a conjectured missing sentence in brackets while retaining the manuscript's visible gap.

explanationMd: Both the bracketed conjecture and a separate digital model make an interpretation available while retaining the distinction between surviving evidence and reconstruction. Silent substitution would erase that distinction.

distractorRationale.d: That repeats the rejected absolute nonintervention rule.
distractorRationale.a: That privileges one state without assessing later evidence.
distractorRationale.b: That removes evidence for future interpretations.
